chains.trait: Opportunistic thermal soaring over broken ground
links: a resident scavenger must patrol a huge home range of broken terrain to find the rare carrion that is its pay
sun heats sunlit rock, scree and cliff faces far faster than valley shade, so those slopes exhale rising thermals while cool ground does not
so the raven flaps between lift sources and glides the legs between them, letting warm air pay for most of the climbing muscle

skill.effect: The raven catches rising air to glide effortlessly over the terrain, covering long distances between rests. It spots carrion from afar while soaring, marking the location for you to follow.

chains.weakness: no sun, no lift: under overcast or rain the indicator goes dark and range halves, and at night it is a slow flapper on the ground where anything can reach it
observe: wings held flat and motionless only while circling above sun-warmed rock
a flap-flap-glide rhythm across a shaded valley, then wings lock open on the next bright slope
a bird losing height over cold water and regaining it the moment it crosses a sunlit scree

journal.en: It buys altitude with sun on stone, and pays in muscle whenever the sun clocks off.

plausibility.summary: 40 km per rest cycle is plausible for dispersing juveniles but not every individual every day; tie long commute to sunny, broken terrain biomes only.
fixes: 40 km per rest cycle is plausible for dispersing juveniles but not every individual every day; tie long commute to sunny, broken terrain biomes only.

links: hundreds of separate stores are each remembered by the landmark beside them
a bird that was watched while hiding returns later and moves the food somewhere else
a store is only worth having if its location stays secret from other minds
and winter food is patchy, frozen and contested, which is what makes hiding worth the memory

skill.effect: The raven quickly locates nearby hidden caches, even those belonging to you, and carries them away. When watched, it shifts its own stash to a new location, causing tracking spells to point to empty ground.

chains.weakness: its memory is landmark-bound: move the stones and it loses its own hoard, and if it knows it is being watched it abandons a good cache, so a visible observer costs it food
observe: a bird pressing food into the ground, then looking up and around
the same morsel reappearing in a different place an hour later
a scatter of small pits under a shrub, most of them empty

journal.en: It hides food from you, then hides the hiding from you.

plausibility.summary: 50 m cache find is strong; frame as landmark vicinity search unless player cache has scent/sign cue. Re-hiding when watched is better documented as strategic recaching under observer risk in corvids broadly.
fixes: 50 m cache find is strong; frame as landmark vicinity search unless player cache has scent/sign cue. Re-hiding when watched is better documented as strategic recaching under observer risk in corvids broadly.

links: a long juvenile period before territory acquisition selects for extended neural plasticity and social learning
this extended apprenticeship requires low-cost rehearsal of precise motor sequences and tolerance thresholds
beak-wrestling and object drop-catch practice aerial tracking, grip control, and partner reliability without injury or caloric waste
this cheap assay of coordination builds cooperative bonds for adult cache defense, though the direct survival payoff remains speculative biology

skill.effect: The raven engages in playful beak-wrestling with a nearby ally, strongly reinforcing their bond and revealing any hidden items or traps in the immediate area. If either bird breaks off the game, they become sharply alert and move with sudden speed for a short while.

chains.weakness: play is loud, slow and conspicuous: a playing pair is distracted and will not flee mid-game, so a stalking predator or player catches both; breaking play costs a turn, so timing it wrong still leaves an opening
observe: two birds gripping each other's beaks and pulling without injury
a stick dropped, caught, carried up and dropped again, over and over
a bird sliding down a snowbank and walking back up to do it again

journal.en: It practises being clever in public and calls it fun.

relations.note: Same fluid physics, inverted solutions. Raven exploits low-density, transparent air for visual soaring and cache retrieval; dolphin exploits high-density, opaque water for active sonar and pressure-resistant diving. Playable: raven's visual tracking counters dolphin's acoustic stealth, while dolphin's sonar pierces raven's visual camouflage in fog.

Grassland mutualism. Ravens follow herds to eat ticks and disturbed insects; pronghorn gain early warning against terrestrial predators. Playable: befriending ravens grants a 'sentinel' alert when pronghorn herds shift direction, revealing hidden water or predators.

Fire exploitation. Ravens drop smoldering twigs into dry grass to flush prey, mimicking human controlled burns. Humans counter with smoke screens and firebreaks to drive ravens from caches. Playable: players can use raven fire-flushing to reveal hidden resources, but must manage smoke drift to avoid alerting rival factions.

Vocal and tool transfer. Humans demonstrate fire-starting and cache-hiding; ravens observe, imitate, and improve the techniques, teaching players how to outsmart spatial traps. Playable: players can learn raven cache-retrieval patterns to find hidden resources, or use human teaching to train raven allies for distraction.
